newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds clamber higher, further gains expected.
newsitem.headline: Bunds clamber higher, further gains expected.

text.p: German Bunds scrambled up to new highs early on Wednesday morning as the view took hold that the rally had not yet petered out.

December Bunds were quoted at a new contract high of 99.18 on the DTB German futures exchange at 0740 GMT, up 13 basis points on the day, and dealers said further gains to 99.25 or 99.30 were possible in the course of the day.
"People are looking for new highs and I don't think we've reached them yet," one Frankfurt-based trader said.
Bunds were propelled on Tuesday by gains in U.S. Treasuries, which closed sharply higher.

The U.S. rally was triggered by a drop in the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index to 51.7 in September from 52.6 in August. The data came in weaker than expected. Treasuries were also boosted by a news report saying Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan sees no immediate inflation threats.

The report, published by the Australian Financial Review on its Internet World Wide Web side, quoted Australia's Treasurer Peter Costello, after a briefing with Greenspan in Washington, as saying Greenspan had indicated to him that he saw no threats of inflation down the track.

Bund dealers in Germany said the market may see some profit-taking ahead of Thursday, when German markets will be closed for the German Unity Day holiday. The market's next focus is the U.S. September payrolls report due on Friday.

"We may see some futures selling ahead of Thursday because some dealers may take Friday off and not be there when the U.S. payroll data come," said Peter Kerger, portfolio manager at Credit Suisse in Frankfurt.
But Kerger added that Bunds were well supported at 99.00. "There's a flow into the German market from abroad with expectations of yields below six percent."
The yield on the benchmark 6.25 percent 10-year Bund was 6.04 percent in early trade. A yield of six percent would be equivalent to a Bund future at 99.40.
Dealers said that once Bunds reached that level the market was likely to take a breather, but one player did not rule out that the rally might eventually propel Bunds to 100.

One dealer saw the trading range for the day at 98.90 to 99.30. U.S. construction spending for August, due out at 1400 GMT, were not expected to prove a big market-mover in European markets, dealers said.
